title: Little Hawley Rising Anew
premise: When the town of Little Hawley exhumes its founder, Nathaniel Hawley, for the bicentennial reinterment, archivist Ada Winterbourne discovers the coffin has been empty for decades—and the crypt's lock was opened with a key kept in the cathedral archive she alone controls. As Detective Ivo Marsh investigates, Ada realizes the killer is using her own meticulously filed records to stage the mystery, framing her as either accomplice or target. Digging into twelve years of sealed correspondence, Ada uncovers that the founder never died in Little Hawley at all: he fled a scandal the town's founding families have protected ever since, and someone is now killing to keep the substitution buried. At the anniversary dinner, Ada traps the killer—the cathedral's own canon, who murdered his predecessor years ago and swapped the body—by baiting him with a falsified ledger entry only the true file-keeper would know was fake. In the aftermath, Ada chooses truth over the town's comfortable silence, finds a found family in Ivo and the unlikely allies who stood by them, and finally steps out of the archive's shadows.
about_author: A. M. Zhou is the pen name of a former parish records volunteer who spent three years cataloguing a decommissioned English church's archives before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about quiet people who know too much, from a drafty house full of unlabeled boxes.

chapters.title: The Weight of Empty Air
chapters.summary: Ada Winterbourne's POV. On the morning of the founder's exhumation, Ada catalogs the ceremony with their usual detached precision, privately dreading the attention it brings to the crypt they've locked for twelve years. When the coffin lid comes up empty, the crowd's gasp lands on Ada like an accusation. Emotional beat: the safe invisibility Ada built begins cracking open.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Alphabetized Silence
chapters.summary: Detective Ivo Marsh arrives and immediately questions how the crypt was accessed; Ada admits the key lives in the archive under their sole control. Flashbacks reveal Ada took the archivist post to disappear after a family disgrace. Emotional beat: fear curdling into defensiveness as Ada realizes they are the obvious suspect.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Doesn't Say
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Searching their own files for tampering, Ada finds a burial record altered in handwriting almost identical to their late predecessor's. Someone knows the archive intimately—but Ada notices one detail wrong: the ink used didn't exist until after the burial date. Emotional beat: dread transforms into the first spark of purpose.

chapters.title: The Canon Who Remembers Everything
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Marsh interviews Canon Edmund Voss, the cathedral's warm, beloved clergyman, who offers helpful historical context and gently suggests Ada's 'instability.' Ivo is charmed but notes Voss answers questions no one asked. Emotional beat: dramatic irony—the reader sees the trap being set around Ada.

chapters.title: A Body That Wasn't Buried
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Following a gap in the 1970s acquisition logs, Ada locates a sealed bequest: letters proving Nathaniel Hawley left town alive decades ago, and that another man was buried in his name. The letters name a witness—Ada's predecessor, who died suddenly. Emotional beat: grief and fury braided together; the archive becomes a weapon.

chapters.title: Anniversary Preparations
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The town hurtles toward the bicentennial dinner while anonymous notes appear warning Ada to 'refile what you found.' Ivo, half-believing in Ada now, proposes an uneasy alliance over bad coffee in the vestry. Emotional beat: loneliness giving way to trust—the first thread of found family.

chapters.title: The Second Key
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada discovers a duplicate crypt key hidden inside a hollowed book of psalms—a gift inscription linking it to Voss's ordination year. Confronting the risk head-on, Ada photographs everything and hides copies with Verity Okafor, the young bell-ringer who has become an unexpected friend. Emotional beat: courage; Ada stops hiding and starts hunting.

chapters.title: Locked In
chapters.summary: Voss's POV, unreliable and chilling. He lures Ada to the crypt after hours, revealing he killed the predecessor who discovered the swap and has been curating the town's myth ever since—he believes the lie is Little Hawley's soul. He locks Ada in among the tombs. Emotional beat: claustrophobic terror; duty and love collide as Ada realizes Ivo will be blamed next.

chapters.title: The Falsified Entry
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, escaping through the ossuary passage only an archivist would know. At the anniversary dinner, Ada publicly announces a 'newly discovered' ledger page—deliberately false—claiming the real burial record survives elsewhere. Voss, unable to bear an uncontrolled document existing, moves to destroy it in front of two hundred witnesses and Ivo. Emotional beat: triumphant reversal; the file-keeper turns filing into a trap.

chapters.title: Reinterment
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, weeks later. With Voss arrested and the founder's true fate told honestly—even though it wounds the town's pride—Ada presides over reburying the unknown man with a truthful stone. Ivo stays in Little Hawley; Verity moves into the archive cottage; Ada, once invisible, signs their name to the new catalog openly. Emotional beat: peace earned—truth chosen over loyalty, family found over solitude.
